lessons.claim: The numerator of the SNR check has to be **the observable's response amplitude and not the driving amplitude**. The chain-bend spec checked a/ℓ_k = 9.83 and passed with a 3.3x margin, but the actual observable is the driven bead's response |ŷ(ω)|, and with the chain and the drag resisting, |ŷ|/ℓ_k falls with ω -- measured at the highest ω it is 0.165, **6x smaller than the thermal fluctuation** (1/60 of the checked value). As a result the Brownian vs Langevin comparison did not even have the power to exclude a difference below 47%. After the fix, 6 of the 7 points turned out to have SNR<3 and 4 of them SNR<1. It is the same hole as trap-drag's 'all 7 hard checks pass and yet the statistics do not come out'.
